Header: Pantoea stewartii syn. Erwinia stewartii Stewart's disease, Stewart's bacterial wilt

Prevention: Bacterial wilt of maize can be transmitted by infected plant material, infected seed and insect vectors:
Use disease-free seed from a certified source.
Manage and control populations of the corn flea beetle, Chaetocnema pulicaria , which is a vector of bacterial wilt.
If available, use resistant maize hybrids or hybrids with moderate or susceptible reactions to bacterial wilt.
Maintain adequate fertilization levels, particularly that of calcium and potassium.
Avoid high levels of nitrogen and phosphorus.
Avoid excess soil moisture as this can make plants more susceptible to the disease.
Monitoring: Monitoring
There are two major phases of bacterial wilt disease: wilt (seen at the seedling stage) and leaf blight (seen after tasselling).
Symptoms:
Seedlings: may rapidly wilt.
Many tillers (branches) may grow from the stem.
Leaves:

Leaf blight - pale-green to yellow, linear streaks with irregular or wavy margins, run parallel to veins along the entire length of the leaf or are limited to 2-3 cm long depending on cultivar resistance.
Leaves: blight symptoms may originate from feeding wounds of the corn flea beetle and so appear dispersed across the leaf.
Tissue around the wounds first becomes water-soaked.
Leaves: pale streaks develop into necrotic tissue.
Premature bleached and dead tassels.
Caveties in the stalks near the soil line.
Kernels may be covered with bacterial slime.
Secondary symptoms such as stalk rot.
Look for the corn flea beetle vector.
Adult: 1.3-3.5 mm long, shiny and black, oval, faint green or blue-bronze shine.
Cut a symptomatic leaf at its base and place in water under a hand lens or microscope to see a yellowish bactieral slime oozing out.
If the corn flea beetle is present in your country, use the
Stevens-Boewe forecast to predict outbreaks of bacerial wilt (as described by
The
American
Phytopathological
Society on http://www.apsnet.org).
Disease symptoms may look similar to: frost damage; drought; nutrient disorders and
Goss's wilt ( Clavibacter michiganensis ssp.
Nebraskensis ).
The disease may be confused with other leaf blights: northern corn leaf blight ( Exserohilum turcicum ); Acidovorax avenae ssp.
Avenae ; Burkholderia andropogonis ; Pantoea ananatis ; Setosphaeria turcica .
Direct Control: There are no effective mechanical, physical or biological control options.
